Full-Time | Brisbane CBD | $80,000 + Superannuation
About Us
Morgan Consulting Engineers (MCE) is an established structural, civil and forensic engineering consultancy that has been operating in Brisbane since 1972.
With around 60 employees across multiple engineering disciplines, we're a friendly, down-to-earth team working across a diverse range of projects. We're looking for an experienced Civil Engineering Draftsperson to join our Civil team in a full-time, office-based position.
The Role
This is a hands-on civil design and drafting role where you'll work closely with our Civil Engineers to develop practical design solutions and produce accurate, coordinated project documentation.
You'll be involved in a variety of civil engineering projects, taking responsibility for allocated design and documentation tasks from initial project information through to engineering review.
Your responsibilities will include:

- Use Civil 3D, PC Drain, PC Sewer, Bluebeam and other relevant civil design software.

- A relevant qualification in Civil Engineering Drafting or a related discipline, and/or demonstrated relevant industry experience.

MCE is an established Brisbane-based engineering consultancy with a collaborative and down-to-earth team environment. Our values are simple: Professionalism + Ethics = Excellence, Teamwork, Enjoy What We Do, Right Solution for the Right Job, and No BS!
Apply Now
This is a full-time, office-based position in our Brisbane office.

About the role
Cono Services is a leading contractor delivering high-profile infrastructure and civil engineering excellence across Australia. Known for innovation, structural integrity, and high safety standards, we pride ourselves on building communities and delivering complex projects on time and within budget. We are seeking an ambitious, analytical, and highly organized Site Engineer to join our project delivery team for a major flagship infrastructure project in the heart of Brisbane cbd. Reporting directly to the Project Manager , you will bridge the gap between design plans and practical onsite execution. You will play an active role in daily operations, ensuring that civil and structural works meet rigid quality standards, safety protocols, and strict timelines.
Key responsibilities
- Site Supervision & Execution

- Maintain accurate project documentation, including daily site diaries, tracking logs, and variation records. 4. Safety & Commercial Management
- Enforce absolute compliance with Australian Work Health and Safety (WHS) regulations, ensuring all personnel wear mandated PPE and adhere to Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS).

Build your career. Lead projects. Deliver infrastructure.
Modern Consultants Pty Ltd is seeking an experienced Senior Civil Engineer / Project Manager to join our growing engineering consultancy based on the Gold Coast.
We provide civil engineering design and project management services to local government and private sector clients, delivering practical engineering solutions across South East Queensland and regional Queensland.
This is an opportunity for an experienced engineer to take ownership of projects, lead technical delivery, manage client relationships and contribute to the continued growth of a developing consultancy.
The Opportunity
The successful applicant will take a leading role in managing and delivering civil infrastructure projects from initial investigations and design through to procurement, construction and completion.
The position offers a diverse workload, combining technical engineering, project management, procurement and construction delivery. You will work directly with clients, contractors, consultants and government stakeholders, with the opportunity to manage projects with a high degree of independence.
Project areas include:
- Road and transport infrastructure upgrades and rehabilitation.
- Stormwater drainage, flood mitigation and water management.
- Bulk earthworks, subdivisions and development infrastructure.
- Civil infrastructure design and construction documentation.
- Local government capital works and regional infrastructure projects.
- Infrastructure procurement, tendering and contract administration.
- Construction supervision and Superintendent services.
Key Responsibilities
Civil Engineering and Technical Leadership
- Lead and undertake civil engineering design, including roads, drainage, earthworks and associated infrastructure.
- Prepare and review engineering calculations, drawings, technical reports and construction documentation.
- Provide technical engineering advice and undertake design reviews to ensure compliance with relevant standards and project requirements.
- Identify technical risks, design constraints and opportunities to improve project outcomes.
Project Management and Delivery
- Manage projects from planning and design through to procurement, construction and completion.
- Develop and manage project scopes, budgets, programs, risk registers and delivery strategies.
- Coordinate consultants, contractors, resources and project stakeholders.
- Monitor project performance and proactively manage technical, commercial and delivery risks.
Procurement and Construction
- Prepare scopes of work, technical specifications, fee proposals and tender documentation.
- Manage tender evaluations, procurement processes and contract administration.
- Review progress claims, variations, contractor submissions and requests for information.
- Undertake construction inspections, provide technical support and oversee delivery against approved designs and specifications.
Client Relationships and Business Development
- Manage client relationships and act as a key point of contact throughout project delivery.
- Prepare proposals, expressions of interest and tender submissions.
- Identify opportunities to develop new client relationships and expand consultancy services.
- Provide practical engineering and project delivery advice to local government and private sector clients.
Leadership and Mentoring
- Provide technical guidance and mentoring to undergraduate, graduate and developing engineers.
- Review engineering work and promote consistent technical and quality standards.
- Contribute to the development of internal processes and the ongoing growth of Modern Consultants.
Qualifications and Experience
Essential:
- Bachelor of Engineering, or an equivalent recognised Civil Engineering qualification.
- Minimum 8 years of relevant professional experience in civil engineering and/or infrastructure project management.
- Demonstrated experience managing civil infrastructure projects from design through to construction.
- Strong technical understanding of road design, stormwater drainage, earthworks and civil infrastructure.
- Experience in project management, procurement, tendering and contract administration.
- Strong written and verbal communication and stakeholder management skills.
- Ability to independently manage projects and take responsibility for technical and commercial outcomes.
- Current driver's licence valid in Queensland.
Desirable:
- Registered Professional Engineer of Queensland (RPEQ), or eligibility to obtain registration.
- Experience working with local government and regional infrastructure projects.
- Experience in construction supervision and Superintendent services.
- Proficiency in AutoCAD, 12D or similar design programs.
- Experience in business development, fee proposals and consultancy tender submissions.
- Experience mentoring and supervising engineering personnel.
About You
You are an experienced civil engineer who combines strong technical capability with practical project management and commercial awareness.
You are comfortable taking ownership of projects, making informed engineering decisions, managing competing priorities and communicating directly with clients and stakeholders.
You take pride in delivering quality engineering outcomes, enjoy working across different project types and are interested in contributing to a growing consultancy where your experience and input can make a genuine difference.
How to Apply
Interested applicants are invited to submit:
- A current resume outlining qualifications and professional experience.
- Details of relevant civil engineering and infrastructure projects delivered.
- Copies of relevant qualifications and professional registrations.
- A brief cover letter outlining suitability for the position.

We operate in a geographically and climatically diverse service area, with sites and locations from Ceduna through to Port Augusta, the Anangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara (APY) Lands, across to the Riverland, down to Mount Gambier, and most places in between.

With nationally and internationally recognised industry expertise, we’re focused on understanding and meeting our customers’ expectations.
As well as safely delivering smart and reliable services for our customers of today, we innovate to shape the water solutions of the future that will support thriving economies and healthy communities.
We are driven by our values; we value our people, we do work that matters, we keep it real, we know that our work has impact and we are future focussed. Staying true to our values ensures that we consistently deliver positive outcomes for all South Australians.

About Newcastle Kill A Pest
Newcastle Kill A Pest is an established locally owned and operated pest management company servicing Newcastle, Lake Macquarie, the Hunter and surrounding areas.
Our work covers a broad range of residential and commercial pest management, including general pest treatments, termite inspections, timber pest management and termite management systems.

We’re looking for someone who wants to become a valued, long-term member of our team.

Depending on your qualifications and experience, your work may include:
- Residential pest management
- Commercial pest management
- General pest inspections and treatments
- Cockroach, ant, spider and other general pest management
- Rodent management
- Termite inspections
- Timber pest inspections
- Termite treatments and management programs
- Installation and servicing of termite management systems
- Preparing job reports and treatment documentation
- Providing customers with practical recommendations and advice
- Managing your daily schedule and allocated jobs
- Maintaining your vehicle, equipment and chemical inventory
- Completing work in accordance with company procedures, product labels and relevant industry requirements
For a trainee, responsibilities will be introduced progressively as your training, qualifications, licensing and competency develop.
If you're an experienced technician
We'd particularly like to hear from you if you have experience in timber pest inspections and termite management.
Ideally, you'll bring experience in some or all of the following:
- General pest management
- Timber pest and termite inspections
- Termite identification and assessment
- Termite treatments
- Chemical soil treatments
- Termite management systems
- Residential and commercial pest management
- Preparing clear and professional inspection reports
- Communicating findings and recommendations to customers
- Managing your own daily workload
- Working independently in the field

If you're looking for a traineeship

We're more interested in finding someone with the right attitude and personal qualities.

- Is reliable and punctual
- Has a strong work ethic
- Is practical and comfortable using tools and equipment
- Communicates confidently with customers
- Presents professionally
- Is comfortable working independently
- Is willing to work in roof voids, subfloors and other confined areas associated with pest management
- Is physically capable of carrying out field-based work
- Is comfortable using mobile technology and completing electronic job reports
- Is willing to learn and take instruction
- Takes pride in doing a job properly
- Wants a long-term career, not simply their next job
People coming from trades, field service, maintenance, landscaping, building, fire services, telecommunications, automotive or similar hands-on industries are encouraged to apply.
The successful trainee will be supported in developing the skills, training and qualifications required to become a professional pest management technician.
What we're looking for
Regardless of whether you're qualified or applying as a trainee, the right person for Newcastle Kill A Pest will be:
- Dependable
- Honest and trustworthy
- Well presented
- Comfortable dealing with customers
- Able to communicate clearly
- Safety conscious
- Able to follow procedures and instructions
- Capable of working both independently and as part of a team
- Organised and able to manage their time
- Comfortable working in different environments each day
- Willing to continue learning and developing their skills

- Company vehicle for work requirements
- Uniform and PPE
- Tools and equipment required for the role

- Ongoing industry training and development
- Support from experienced pest management technicians
- Variety across residential and commercial pest management
- Opportunity to develop specialist termite and timber pest skills
- A genuine long-term career pathway within the business

Remuneration

Life at Fulton Hogan is about making the most of opportunities, taking responsibility, and making it happen. We appreciate our peoples' courage, curiosity and unique perspectives, and look to collaborate as much as possible to explore safer, smarter and more efficient ways of working in this rapidly changing world. We don't stand still - there are always opportunities to do more and do better.
Keen to progress your career? Take full advantage of our tailored training, leadership, and mentoring programs; or leverage our partnerships with industry association such as Engineers Australia, Chartered Accountants, CPA Australia, Infrastructure Sustainability Council, The National Association of Women in Construction, plus many more.
Looking to enhance your wellbeing? We will encourage you to explore flexible working arrangements where possible. We offer great benefits, including corporate health and fitness programs, health insurance discounts, personal banking support, a range of retailer discounts, up to 18 weeks paid primary carers parental leave and up to 10 days paid secondary carers leave, access to our Employee Assistance Program (including your immediate family), and the option to take more time for yourself throughout the year with our Purchase Leave Policy.
Want to help us better the communities we live and work in? Our purpose of creating, connecting, and caring for communities is more than a saying to us - it's a way of thinking, working, and living because we're locals too, and seek to give back in ways that strengthen and build resilient communities. We do this because we genuinely care, enjoy what we do, and even manage to have some fun along the way! You'll find us partnering with local and national community groups, like Clontarf Foundation, Black Dog Institute, and Soldier On, in addition to indigenous groups and social enterprises, to ensure that our good work positively impacts and brings about sustainable change within our industry.
Do we offer a 'competitive' salary package? Of course! Speak to our Talent Acquisition or People & Culture team to learn more.
What's on offer?
Fulton Hogan - Infrastructure Services, is seeking an experienced Project Engineer to support the Civils team based in either the Sunshine Coast or Gold Coast, Queensland.
Reporting to the Project Manager (PM) or Senior Project Engineer (SPE) this role will see you play a crucial part in developing and delivering various minor civil projects in the region on time, within budget and to a high standard of safety and quality. You will build on our strong key stakeholder relationships within both the government and private sectors, and you will be empowered to lead and develop a team of Site Engineers and Graduate Engineer to ensure successful project delivery within a safety-first culture.
This position may require some local and regional state travel as per individual project requirements.
Your key responsibilities will include:
- Planning and coordinating works to ensure they are carried out in compliance to all health and safety, quality, and environmental legislation and company procedures and assist PM / SPE in the delivery of civil construction projects.
- Drive a safety-first approach across the department in line with Fulton Hogan's "Living Safely" Culture and WHS Legislation.
- Attend project meetings and report on project performance and manage cost control tracking, monitoring productivities and forecasting costs to complete for end of month reviews.
- Contract management across multiple packages of works with ability to identify variations/EOTs and prepare submission to clients.
- Read and interpret drawings and prepare subcontract packages and administer to fulfil site requirement.
- Utilise programming software to develop and maintain short term programs in consultation with field operations.
- Support tender submission with a sound working knowledge of plant capability and civil productivities.
How will you connect to the role?
You will possess a Degree in Civil Engineering with proven experience in pavement and civil construction, with TMR experience as advantageous, although not essential.
Your ability to manage multiple packages of work at once and to identify and address issues before they arise will set you up for success. Your analytical ability in cost control, reviewing monthly project forecasts and interrogating forecasting costs to complete as required, will also be crucial to your delivery. Your capability in maintaining positive client relationships and ensuring contractual obligations are met will lead to positive outcomes for the department. A valid driver's licence is essential for this position.
This position may require state-wide travel subject to project scope.
Our people share the same set of values that keep us REAL. Respect, Energy and Effort, Attitude and Leadership encapsulate what we stand for at Fulton Hogan and encourage us to foster a diverse and inclusive culture where we listen to, care for, celebrate, and respect everyone.
We are committed to reconciliation and building and nurturing respectful relationships with First Nations peoples. Through our First Nations Engagement Strategy and Reconciliation Action Plan (RAP), we aim to promote opportunities, cultural understanding and partnerships that celebrate and acknowledge the contributions of Indigenous communities.
If our values resonate with you, please submit an application for the position. If you're not sure that you meet 100% of the selection criteria, that's okay, we would still like to hear from you and potentially discuss how your skills could be utilised at Fulton Hogan.
For over 90 years, Fulton Hogan has been delivering high-quality infrastructure to improve the lives of people every day. Our 10,000+ team works in every kind of weather and environment, creating, connecting, and caring for communities across Australia, New Zealand, and the South Pacific.

IOR might be the greatest Aussie success story you haven’t heard of… yet.
From humble roots in Eromanga, QLD, we’ve been fuelling the furthest corners of Australia for over 40 years. But we think the most exciting journey’s still on the horizon.
Joining IOR means stepping into a role where your work genuinely matters. Working across the full project lifecycle, from design and procurement through to construction and commissioning, you'll combine technical expertise with practical project delivery to help ensure safe, compliant, and high-performing aviation fuel facilities. This is an opportunity to contribute to a growing business while working on critical infrastructure that keeps Australia moving.
About the role
This role supports the delivery of aviation fuel infrastructure projects by providing technical engineering expertise, project management support, and stakeholder coordination. You'll work closely with internal teams, contractors, consultants, and airport stakeholders to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, and in compliance with industry standards.
- Lead and support aviation fuel infrastructure projects through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational handover.

- Collaborate with airport authorities, regulators, consultants, and operational teams to deliver successful project outcomes.
What you'll bring
You'll bring strong engineering capability, project delivery experience, and a practical approach to solving complex infrastructure challenges. You're comfortable working with stakeholders at all levels, balancing technical requirements with commercial outcomes, and ensuring projects are delivered safely and compliantly.
- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Project Management, or a related discipline, with a current driver's licence and willingness to travel.
- Experience delivering fuel infrastructure, aviation fuelling, bulk liquids storage, or similar industrial projects.
- Strong knowledge of AS 1940, AS 1692, JIG standards, and engineering risk management processes.
- Proven ability to manage contractors, commissioning activities, project schedules, budgets, and stakeholder relationships.
- Excellent communication, commercial acumen, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work across multiple business functions.
Why join IOR?
Approaching each day through our values of Innovation finding solutions, Our Communities serving people, and Reliability getting results, our team is focused on delivering what really matters to our customers. It’s this mindset that drives us forward. We’re about so much more than fuel. We’re about three key things:
- 
Right Team: It’s the kind of place where you walk in the door and instantly know you belong
- 
Right Track: We’re going somewhere, and as we get bigger, so do the opportunities to get stuck in and challenge yourself
- 
Right Now: There’s no dragging feet or endless committees here. We deliver for Australia every single day
You’ll also be rewarded with a range of benefits, including:
- Grow your expertise and career with access to experienced mentors and ongoing training and development opportunities
- Team member and family discounts on fuel (obviously!)
- Work hard, play hard with our Blue Squad social club – trivia nights, barbecues and plenty of laughs!
- Plus salary sacrificing options, retail and health care discounts, Employee Assistance Program, and much more
Ready to go further with us?
If this sounds like you, don’t overthink it - just apply! We look forward to meeting you.

- Experience managing gas drainage activities and underground drilling programs.
- Ability to manage contractors to deliver safe, timely and cost-effective outcomes.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a focus on system performance and continuous improvement.
- Strong commitment to safety, compliance and operational excellence.
- Strong work ethic with the ability to work collaboratively across technical and operational teams.
- Proactive approach with the ability to take ownership and deliver results in a dynamic underground mining environment.
WHY ARGO?

- Ideally this position suits someone based in the Moranbah, Mackay, Airlie Beach area or someone willing to relocate.
- Accommodation is provided and flexible based on your home location.
- Attractive remuneration and other benefits available with career progression opportunities.
